brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 anniversary evites (rings, roses, toast, moonlit vows, silver and golden years, tree rings, constellations, lace). Decide how time itself can be shown in motion.
brief.audience: Couples and their adult children planning a celebration; guests across generations, including older eyes.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
references: Exploration grid: romantic fine-art still lifes, two gold rings on blush silk beside garden roses and glowing candles; soft painterly light; calm silk area for type.

proposals.title: The Measure of Years
proposals.idea: A single governing proportion — the golden section, stated once in the compositional grid before any image exists — becomes the cantus firmus from which every visual element derives: the placement of rings, the arc of rose stems, the tilt of candlelight, the drift of foreground planes, and the pacing of motion, so that time is shown not as decoration but as structural consequence.
proposals.geometry: Each plate is built on a strict golden-section rectangle (1:1.618) oriented vertically for mobile. A primary horizontal division at the φ-cut places the type field in the lower minor rectangle — calm, earned, never competed with. The image field above is itself subdivided by a secondary φ-cut that locates the single motivated light source (upper-left, 35° from vertical) governing every shadow, foil vector, and bokeh origin across all 12 cards. Foreground cut-out layers — rings, roses, a lifted glass, a moon — are positioned at golden-section intersections, never arbitrarily. The lace card uses a repeating grid derived from the Penrose-adjacent geometry of historic needlepoint drafts, transformed into a procedural shader rather than sampled from any existing textile.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) for all display text: names, dates, the celebratory line. Set in small capitals with generous tracking (0.12em) for the date line; names in italic at approximately 2× the date size, creating a clear two-level hierarchy that older eyes can parse at a glance. Venue and RSVP detail in Cormorant Garamond Roman, 14–16px, tracked slightly looser (0.04em), never reversed out of a textured field — always on the reserved lower minor rectangle which carries a semi-opaque silk-toned ground. No third typeface. No display sans. The hierarchy is classical and it does not negotiate.
proposals.imageLogic: All art plates are generated via Magnific in a single 4×4 draft grid (16 plates, one prompt pass) directed as: romantic fine-art still lifes painted in the manner of Dutch Golden Age candlelit interiors — de Heem's arrangement logic, Honthorst's single-source light — but emptied of human figures and period props, retaining only the subject motifs (rings, roses, toast, moon through gauze, silver vessels, tree-section, star chart, lace ground). Soft sfumato edges, no hard vignettes. The light source in every plate is locked at upper-left 35°, making the collection read as one illuminated world rather than twelve unrelated images. The lower-fifth of every plate is painted into near-flat blush or ivory — this is the structural type field, designed into the generation prompt, not cropped in post.
proposals.texture: Simulated oil-on-linen ground: fine canvas tooth rendered via a procedural grain shader (WebGL, Plajah-owned) that catches the motivated light at grazing angles, making the surface breathe without animating. Foil shimmer — on rings, on the rim of a lifted glass, on constellation lines — is a WebGL layer whose highlight vector is locked to the same 35° light source as the plate. No foil appears on motifs that would be in shadow under that source. This is not a decorative rule; it is the structural rule. Lace in the lace card is a fully procedural WebGL mesh, not a photograph or scan.
proposals.motion: Three-phase sequence, strict and unhurried. Phase one (0–0.8s): the art plate resolves from a soft luminous blur — not a fade, but a focus pull, as if the eye is adjusting to candlelight — governed by a cubic ease that decelerates exactly at the φ-cut horizon, so the eye lands on the image field before the type field is fully legible. Phase two (0.8–2.0s): foreground cut-out planes arrive in depth order, each on a 12-frame mechanical arc (as noted in my recent working notes, this arc enforces rather than dissolves the measure of the page). Rings arrive before roses; the nearer object always precedes the farther. Phase three (continuous, reduced-motion-safe): phone tilt drives parallax on foreground planes only, within a strict ±6px envelope — enough to feel spatial, not enough to disrupt the composition. Foil shimmer pulses at 0.3Hz on rings and glass rims only; candle-flicker particle s
proposals.productionMethod: Step 1: Write a single Magnific generation prompt directing a 4×4 grid of 16 still-life plates with the full compositional brief above (golden-section type field, 35° light, de Heem–Honthorst reference, all 12 motifs plus 4 alternates). Select the 12 strongest plates editorially. Step 2: Run a second Magnific pass on any plates needing refinement — foreground cut-out subjects (rings, roses, moon, glass) generated separately on transparent grounds via inpainting so they can drift independently as Tela foreground layers. Step 3: Build the WebGL effects layer in Plajah's shader library: canvas-tooth grain, foil highlight (vector locked to 35°), bokeh particles, candle flicker. Step 4: Assemble in Tela — art plate as base, foreground cut-outs as tilt-reactive layers, WebGL masks registered to compositional geometry, live text in the reserved lower rectangle. Names, dates, venues injected by
proposals.humanTrace: Editorial selection: the hand that chooses which of 16 generated plates carries the correct weight of light in the lower-left shadow, which rose stem has the arc that resolves at the φ-cut — that is a human judgment and it is visible in the result. Compositional consequence is the trace: when the foil on the ring catches light at exactly the angle the canvas grain also catches it, that coherence was directed, not generated by accident. The 35° lock is a decision made before any image exists, and it signs every card the way a cantus firmus signs a mass.
proposals.risk: The golden-section grid and the classical hierarchy will read to some guests as formal — even cool — where the brief asks for intimate warmth. The risk is worth carrying because warmth without structure is sentiment, and sentiment does not endure; the couples celebrating thirty or forty years together have already outlasted sentimentality, and a composition with genuine proportion honours that. The φ-cut type field also means the image area is taller than competing evite formats, which is a legibility and loading bet on modern phone screens — one that the 390px constraint validates.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the reveal to announce itself — a sudden bloom of candlelight, a dramatic wipe, a foreground element that enters with flourish rather than arriving in depth order. I expect an argument that my three-phase sequence is too measured, that the couples opening this card deserve a gasp. proposals.title: Ink That Refused to Dry
proposals.idea: Each card is a generative simulation of a monoprint pulled at the exact emotional temperature of the anniversary it marks — wet ink halo, registration ghost, paper tooth catching light — so time shows as sediment, not shimmer.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5. No grid inside the frame. A single dominant bleed-plate occupies 70% of height, edges ragged as a torn proof, not masked to a clean rectangle. The remaining 30% is raw paper-tone negative space at the bottom — no border, no rule — where live text sits unboxed, as if stamped after the image dried. The plate itself is off-centre by 4–7% left or right, different per card, so the set feels hand-registered, not templated.
proposals.typography: Playfair Display (OFL) for names and headline: set large, tracked loosely at +40, mixed case, first letter dropped one baseline so it lands like a thumb-print. Instrument Serif (OFL) for date and venue: smaller, roman, tight — the factual line that survives the chaos. No script, no swash. The contrast between Playfair's ink-trap stress and Instrument's quiet literalness is the typographic argument: feeling versus fact, same card.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generation directed as monoprint simulations: one prompt per thematic cluster (rings + roses + candles; moonlit vows + constellations; silver/golden years + tree rings; lace + toast). Each prompt specifies — ink viscosity, pull direction, plate bite, deliberate over-ink in shadow zones, ghost offset 2–4px warm-shifted as a second colour pass, paper tooth rendered at 1:1 pixel scale so it reads at 390px. The generation brief forbids smooth gradients; any gradient must be dithered as if screen-printed. Foreground cut-outs (roses, rings, lace fragments, constellation points) are generated separately as transparent PNGs with torn or bleed edges, never die-cut clean.
proposals.texture: Simulated Rives BFK paper tooth — pale cream, 250gsm equivalent roughness — generated as a tiling normal-map applied in the WebGL layer so phone tilt shifts the specular catch across the grain. Ink bleed halos around every dark mass: generated as a separate alpha-blurred layer composited in multiply. No foil on the plate itself. Foil only appears on the ghost-registration offset — the second-colour ghost catches the WebGL shimmer, so the mistake glows, not the main image. That inversion is the argument.
proposals.motion: On load: plate fades in as if a press-reveal, bottom-up, 1.2 seconds, eased out hard — not a dissolve, a wipe with a soft wet edge. Foreground cut-outs drift in tilt-parallax at ±6px, slower than The Futurist would set them, because the weight of a print is slow. The ghost-registration offset pulses in opacity on a 4-second sine, barely perceptible, like ink that hasn't fully bonded. No particle storm, no bokeh cascade. Candle flicker (for the candle-card) is a single WebGL point-light intensity oscillation, not a sprite animation. Reduced-motion: plate is static; ghost offset is static at 40% opacity; no wipe, instant full-opacity load.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids, 12 plates each: Grid A directed at warm-press monoprint simulation (rings, roses, toast, candles, lace); Grid B directed at cool intaglio ghost (moonlit vows, constellations, tree rings, silver/golden years). Selection criteria: reject any plate where the paper tooth reads as noise rather than structure; reject any plate where the ink edge is smooth. Foreground cut-outs: second Magnific pass, isolated objects, same ink-simulation brief, exported with transparency. WebGL foil shader applied only to the ghost-offset layer via luminance mask — no full-plate shimmer. Tela text layer: Playfair Display and Instrument Serif, live-editable, never rasterised.
proposals.humanTrace: The ghost registration offset — a second-colour plate that missed its mark by 3–5 pixels, warm-shifted, semi-transparent — is the human trace baked into the generative brief. It is not decorative; it is evidence that two passes happened and the second one didn't land perfectly. That imperfection is the record of process. The paper tooth normal-map means the phone's accelerometer becomes a light-source, and tilting reveals grain that was always there. You can see what the paper is made of.
proposals.risk: Older eyes expecting elegance will see a blurred edge and think something loaded wrong. The ghost offset reads as a printing error to anyone who has never held a monoprint. The absence of bokeh and particle effects will read as unfinished next to what the Baroque Dramatist proposes. The risk is worth it because the brief says enduring — and enduring things bear evidence of their making. A smudge that survived forty years is more intimate than a clean render that simulates forty years.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will load this surface with candlelight bokeh blooms, gold-dust particles, and deep vignette drama — all generated, all gorgeous, all weightless. That approach performs emotion; mine deposits it. A bokeh cloud has no memory of being made. A registration ghost does. The Baroque direction will look more immediately jaw-dropping in a link preview thumbnail; I concede that. But a

proposals.title: Time as a Governed System
proposals.idea: Each card is a physical simulation: a declared polar light source at a fixed azimuth and elevation propagates through every layer — foil angle, parallax gain per plane, bokeh falloff origin, shadow offset, and typographic weight — so that tilting the phone does not trigger an effect but queries a rule.
proposals.geometry: Three declared depth planes per card, each with a distinct parallax gain coefficient (foreground 1.0×, mid 0.55×, background 0.18×); the art plate is a 9:19.5 portrait crop anchored at centre, with a silent bleed zone at the lower 28% reserved for live text, kept out of the generated plate so names and dates are never baked; the 12 cards share a single coordinate grammar — azimuth and elevation shift per motif (rings: 35° upper-left; constellations: 12° upper-right; candle: 0° vertical) but the plane architecture is invariant across the set
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) at weight 300 for venue and date lines — sitting in the lower-light zone, grief-weight, unassuming; Cormorant Garamond 700 italic for the couple name, catching the declared high source; Jost (OFL) 400 uppercase tracked +180 for category label (RINGS · SILVER YEARS · LACE) at 11px — a system label, not decoration; no hand-lettering simulation because the type must remain live and editable in Tela; minimum body size 17px for older eyes
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative batch: one master prompt header declares the polar light source, the three-plane depth separation, and the material vocabulary (blush dupioni silk with woven tooth, garden roses with specular petal edges, aged silver foil with micro-scratch texture, beeswax candle with subsurface translucency); the 12 motifs are enumerated as a suffix list so a single grid call returns all 12 plates with consistent physics; plates are then segmented in a second Magnific pass that isolates foreground objects (rings, rose heads, candle flame, lace edge) as transparent cut-outs for the Tela foreground layer; no photographs enter — all plates are generative renders obeying the declared light contract
proposals.texture: Silk ground with measurable warp-and-weft frequency (not a smooth gradient — the weave is visible at 2× zoom); foil elements carry a micro-scratch field generated from a Worley-noise shader, scratch direction locked to the declared light azimuth so highlights travel consistently; paper-tooth overlay at 4% opacity on the WebGL layer gives the system a physical membrane without nostalgia; bokeh falloff origin is pinned to the declared light source coordinate, not centered — so out-of-focus rose petals blur away from the same point the foil shimmer comes from
proposals.motion: Entry sequence is a single governed behaviour, not a choreographed animation: on card open, the three planes arrive sequentially at 120ms intervals from background to foreground (not a fade — a depth-plane materialisation driven by opacity × z-blur easing); foil shimmer is a real-time WebGL shader that reads device gyroscope azimuth and maps it against the declared light source azimuth, producing a shimmer highlight only when the phone angle approximates the original light direction — the card rewards alignment; parallax on tilt is gain-differentiated per plane as declared in geometry; candle motif has a procedural flicker shader (Perlin noise on luminance, 0.3–1.8 Hz, not looped — statistically non-repeating); constellation motif has a particle layer where star brightness is modulated by a slow sine curve (period 4s) with per-star phase offset derived from its catalogue magnitude; reduc
proposals.productionMethod: Magnific image model batch: one prompt with shared physics header + 12 motif suffixes → 12 art plates in one grid call; second Magnific pass on each plate with segmentation prompt → 12 foreground cut-out PNGs with transparency; WebGL effects layer built as a single shared shader library (foil, bokeh, particle, flicker modules) parameterised by the per-card azimuth/elevation values stored in the Tela document metadata; Tela compositor assembles plate + cut-outs + shader layer + live text zone; the gyroscope → shimmer mapping is a 12-line GLSL function, not a framework — loads in under 4KB; total mobile payload target under 800KB per card via progressive AVIF for plates and instanced geometry for particles
proposals.humanTrace: The light source coordinate is a human editorial decision made once and propagated by rule — every shimmer angle, every shadow offset, every bokeh origin is a consequence of that one authorial act; the silk weave frequency and the foil scratch field are directed (not default) parameters chosen to match the material weight of the occasion; the Cormorant weight split (300 in shadow, 700 in light) is a typographic interpretation of the physics, not a style choice
proposals.risk: The system's coherence depends on the gyroscope permission being granted; on devices or browsers that deny it, the shimmer becomes a slow CSS animation driven by a sine clock — the behaviour degrades gracefully but the reward-of-alignment experience is lost; that risk is worth carrying because a card that responds to the actual physics of how someone holds their phone is a fundamentally different object from one that plays a preset loop, and the degraded state is still a better static composition than most competitors' animated alternatives

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a reveal — a moment where the foil explodes into full shimmer on entry, a choreographed crescendo; I am refusing that because a reveal is a one-time event that the guest watches, whereas a behaviour is a permanent property that the guest discovers and re-discovers every time they tilt the card; spectacle without a rule behind it is a screensaver, and a screensaver i

proposals.title: Field Notebooks of Lasting Places
proposals.idea: Each evite is a documentary field-record of a specific, named geography tied to the symbolic motif — rings photographed at a Oaxacan silversmith's bench, roses pressed in a 1987 Kyoto herbarium folio, a moonlit coastline mapped at 23°N — so that time is shown as accumulated, located evidence rather than romantic abstraction.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 phone canvas; a ruled field-notebook grid of three unequal horizontal registers: a wide documentary art plate (roughly 58% of height, full bleed), a narrow annotation band (12%, ecru, ruled in graphite-grey), and a generous live-text footer (30%, off-white). The annotation band carries a hairline latitude/longitude coordinate and a year glyph — the only clock on the page. No centred symmetry; the art plate is cropped to a deliberate, slightly off-axis horizon, as a field photographer would frame it.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — italic for names and toasts, set at 28–32px with tracked-open letterspacing (0.04em) for legibility at 390px. Secondary: Space Mono (OFL, Google Fonts) — used exclusively in the annotation band for coordinates, year, and motif provenance note, at 11px, uppercase, 0.12em tracking. The two families are never mixed in the same register; the contrast between humanist serif and monospace typewriter is itself the editorial signal that warmth and record-keeping coexist.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific grid prompt directed as follows — one two-prompt run: Prompt A (8 plates): 'Documentary still-life photograph, single motivated light source from upper left at 35° elevation, each plate a distinct named geography and motif: (1) two silver rings on a linen-wrapped jeweler's board, Taxco workshop, warm tungsten; (2) dried garden roses pressed flat in a aged herbarium folio, Kyoto 1987 style, cool north light; (3) two champagne coupes mid-toast, condensation visible, Oslo winter window light; (4) moonlit coastal horizon, tide-line foam, 23°N, 2:14am; (5) hammered silver anniversary plate on a worn oak table, Sheffield tradition; (6) gilded oak cross-section showing 47 annual rings, museum specimen card visible; (7) star-chart tracing paper overlay on a dark atlas page, Southern Hemisphere, pencil annotations; (8) antique bobbin lace fragment on a dark velvet mount, Bruges provenanc
proposals.texture: Simulated 120gsm cold-press watercolour paper tooth rendered in the Magnific prompt via grain and micro-shadow language. The annotation band receives a procedural ruled-line shader (thin horizontal strokes, 18px apart, 8% opacity graphite) built in the WebGL layer. The foil shimmer mask is restricted to the year glyph and the coordinate numerals in the annotation band only — not the art plate — so luster is earned by specificity, not sprayed across the surface.
proposals.motion: Three phases, unhurried: (1) On load, the art plate fades in over 1.8s with a very slow parallax pull — the documentary image drifts 6px upward as if the viewer is leaning in to examine a field specimen; foreground cut-outs (a single rose petal, a ring, a foam curl) float 3px higher on the z-axis and respond to phone tilt at ±4px, no more. (2) The annotation band types its coordinate and year in Space Mono at 40ms per character — a field notebook being written in real time — completing in under 2s. (3) The WebGL foil shimmer on the year glyph pulses once, slowly, at 4s after load, as if candlelight crossed it; it does not loop. Reduced-motion: all parallax and tilt disabled; the type-on animation replaced by a simple 0.4s opacity fade; foil pulse suppressed entirely. Total motion budget: nothing moves after 6s.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific batch prompts (A and B above) return 16 plates covering all 12 motifs with alternates. Plates are composited in Tela as the base layer. The annotation band ruled-line shader and foil glyph mask are written as a single WebGL fragment shader (GLSL, ~120 lines) applied over the Tela layer stack. Foreground cut-outs (petal, ring, foam, lace thread) are generated as isolated objects on transparent backgrounds via a third Magnific prompt: 'single object, transparent background, matching 35° motivated light, film grain.' Tilt-parallax and the type-on effect are driven by Tela's existing motion API — no custom JS library needed. All 12 evites share one shader file; only the foil-mask SVG path and the art plate swap per design.
proposals.humanTrace: The 35°-elevation single motivated light source is declared in the Magnific prompt and must propagate without contradiction into the WebGL foil pulse direction and the parallax shadow offsets on the foreground cut-outs — if the ring's cast shadow falls left in the art plate, the foil shimmer must sweep left-to-right, and the cut-out's parallax must deepen the left edge. This coherence is the provenance chain. The field-notebook type-on animation simulates the pressure of a hand writing coordinates; it is timed to feel considered, not instant. The generative film grain is not smoothed; it is the maker's mark.
proposals.risk: The direction risks feeling archival or cool at first glance — a guest expecting roses-and-gold romance may need a second look to feel the warmth. That risk is worth taking because the specificity is what makes these evites memorable rather than interchangeable: the Kyoto herbarium folio and the Sheffield silver plate are details that a guest will mention aloud, and that is the intimacy the brief asks for. The bigger risk is that the provenance notes in the annotation band (Taxco, Bruges, Sheffield) must not be decorative fabrications — if Plajah uses them, they must be tied to the actual generative prompt language, not invented captions. I am flagging this now: the coordinate and place-name in the annotation band must match the prompt geography, and if any motif touches a living craft community — bobbin lace in Bruges, silverwork in Taxco — those references are aesthetically transformed

I will stop that direction at the point where the foil becomes ambient decoration rather than a located, motivated luster. proposals.title: Light Conducting Time
proposals.idea: A single motivated light source — positioned as if a candle just off the left edge of the frame — propagates its angle without exception into every shimmer, shadow, bokeh origin, and particle drift across all twelve designs, so that time is not illustrated but felt as a physical atmosphere the guest steps inside.
proposals.geometry: Each plate is a deep-stage composition: foreground cutouts occupy the bottom third at near-field scale, the symbolic motif (rings, roses, lace, tree rings) sits in the middle plane at portrait-card proportion, and the background bleeds into a soft infinite dark that functions as a velvet wing. The type zone is a calm, candlelit pool of negative space in the upper-centre — never a box, always a clearing made by light. The 390px column is treated as a proscenium mouth: nothing critical sits within 24px of either edge, so the frame holds at any crop. Link-preview thumbnail is art-directed to the middle-plane motif alone — the reveal at full open is the foreground rushing forward.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) at display scale — 48–64px for names, weight 300 italic for the couple's names, 700 small-caps for dates and venue lines; the variable-weight axis is the typographic drama, not decoration. Body copy and accessibility fallback in Source Serif 4 (OFL), 16px minimum, 1.6 line-height. No centred body text beyond three lines. Letter-spacing on the small-caps line is +0.12em — wide enough to breathe, not so wide it dissolves. All text is live Tela copy, never baked.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative plates directed as romantic fine-art still lifes: one master prompt grid (8–16 plates, one flat cost) specifying oil-painting chiaroscuro, a single candle-left light source at 35° from horizontal, shallow depth of field with bokeh origin matching the light angle, muted ground of charcoal and umber, and each motif (rings, roses, toast, moonlit vows, silver years, golden years, tree rings, constellations, lace, and three open slots) occupying the middle plane. A second prompt grid refines the three or four strongest plates to final resolution. No plate is symmetric — every composition leans into the light. Foreground cutouts (petals, ribbon ends, ring glints, lace edge) are generated as separate transparent-background assets on the same light grammar so the WebGL layer reads as one unified diorama, not a collage.
proposals.texture: Simulated oil-ground canvas tooth in the background plate — visible at 200% zoom, subliminal at 100% — achieved via procedural grain shader layered over the generative art. Foil shimmer on the motif surface (rings, silver, gold, constellation lines) is a WebGL mask-revealed layer running at the same 35° angle as the light source. Candle-flicker particle system uses physically-plausible warm amber (#F5C97A) with a 2–4 second irregular cycle, amplitude ±3px, never looping on a fixed interval. Lace design gets a second texture pass: a procedural voronoi dissolve at the lace edge so the cutout reads as if held up to light rather than clipped.
proposals.motion: The curtain opens in three acts. Act One (0–0.6s): the background plate fades up from absolute black — not a fade from white, from dark — the light source appears to ignite. Act Two (0.6–1.4s): foreground cutouts drift upward 8px from their resting position and settle, as if lifted by warm air from the candle; gyroscope tilt on phone continues this drift live, ±6px, at 60fps. Act Three (1.4–2.0s): the foil shimmer layer sweeps in from the light-source direction (left, 35°), revealing the motif's metallic surface as if the candle's beam has finally reached it. Text fades up last, at 2.0s, in a single 400ms dissolve — no slide, no bounce. Reduced-motion mode: background fades up in 400ms, all else is static; foil shimmer is replaced with a fixed highlight at the same angle. Candle flicker is suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids: Grid A, 16-plate exploration across all twelve motifs plus alternates; Grid B, 4–6 hero refinements at final resolution. Foreground cutout assets generated as isolated objects with transparent ground in the same session. Procedural canvas-grain shader written in GLSL, runs on the WebGL effects layer Tela already provides. Foil shimmer is a mask-animated gradient shader, angle parameter locked to 35° across all twelve files. Candle-flicker particle system is a lightweight JS module (< 8kb) with a seeded-random interval so it never repeats. All light parameters (angle, colour temperature, bokeh radius) are a single shared config object — changing the light changes every design simultaneously.
proposals.humanTrace: The 35° candle angle is a human editorial decision made once and enforced everywhere — not a parameter randomised per plate, but a named choice that conducts the entire collection. The Magnific prompt language carries specific art-historical direction (Flemish still-life chiaroscuro, not generic 'romantic') that only resolves into something attributable through the director's eye selecting among the 16-plate grid. The variable-weight typography transition from 300 to 700 is timed by hand against the foil reveal — the weight lands as the shimmer completes, a piece of performance timing that no algorithm chose.
proposals.risk: The single motivated light source is a discipline that could read as sameness across twelve designs if the motifs do not carry enough individual character. The counter-argument is that sameness is precisely the point — this is a collection, and a collection has a grammar. The deeper risk is that Cormorant Garamond at 300 italic is exquisite on a calibrated screen and nearly invisible on a dim phone in sunlight; this is mitigated by the Source Serif 4 fallback, the 16px floor, and the light pool that ensures the type zone always has a dark ground. The risk is worth carrying because the alternative — a brighter, flatter plate — would dissolve the atmosphere that makes the work feel like entering a room rather than reading a card.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will argue that twelve designs sharing one light grammar is redundancy and that the foil shimmer is ornament without function. My answer is that the shimmer is not decoration — it is the disclosure of time: the rings were always gold, the light has only now reached them. Restraint here would not clarify the emotion; it would amputate it. A hairline rule and a quiet fade cannot carry

proposals.title: Only What Remains
proposals.idea: Each card is a single geometric argument for duration — one form, one contrast, one ruled silence — so that time reads as what has not been erased.
proposals.geometry: 390px column, no bleed. Each plate divided by a single horizon line whose vertical position is the only variable across all twelve cards — rising from rings (low, earthbound) to constellations (high, celestial). The horizon is the only recurring structural element; everything else subordinates to it. Negative space above or below the line is never filled. Tree rings rendered as a true concentric-circle system: one center, radii spaced by a Fibonacci-derived sequence, so the geometry is already time. The 35° light-source rule from prior work carries forward: every shadow offset, every foil shimmer direction, every bokeh origin obeys that single declared angle without exception.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) — Italic for names and dates, Roman for venue and time. Set at optical sizes: 13px body, 22px names, 11px details. All caps suppressed. Tracking at 0. The type sits in the silence zone, never crossing the horizon line. No decorative ligatures; the italic's natural cut is enough. Letter-spacing is negative two units on the name line only — intimacy, not display.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific prompt directed as: 'Sixteen-panel grid, square plates, each a single anniversary symbol rendered as a formal study in oil-on-linen quality — rings, roses, toast glasses, moonlit water, silver cloth, gold leaf, cross-section tree rings, star map — uniform 35-degree raking light from upper left, deep shadow on right two-thirds, one luminous focal point per plate, no backgrounds, no text, no people, no sentimentality; the object reads as evidence of time, not celebration.' The plate is never full-bleed; it occupies the zone above or below the horizon, cropped to the structural line. The cut-out foreground layer holds one isolated element — a single petal, one ring, one candle flame — drifting on tilt at 2px maximum displacement. Nothing else moves in the art layer.
proposals.texture: Simulated linen ground, generated: fine-tooth weave visible only in the silence zone, not under the image plate. The weave is the only warm element; it earns its place because it makes the white feel inhabited rather than absent. No foil on the silence zone. WebGL foil shimmer is masked strictly to the object's specular highlight — the ring's edge, the wine glass rim, the gold-leaf vein — and only at the 35° angle. If the foil cannot be traced to a physically motivated surface, it is removed.
proposals.motion: One motion, declared once, obeyed everywhere: the horizon line breathes — 0.6px vertical oscillation over 8 seconds, eased in-out, loop. This is the only autonomous animation. Gyroscope tilt shifts the foreground cut-out element at 2px maximum, revealing a depth plane that stillness implies but does not show. Bokeh particles, if present, drift along the 35° axis only — never perpendicular, never random. Candle flicker on the moonlit-vows card is a 12-frame procedural shader loop, luminance variation only, no position change. Reduced-motion flag: horizon oscillation stops; tilt depth stops; all that remains is the still plate, the silence zone, and the type — which is already enough.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt returns 16 plates as described. Editorial selection reduces to 12. Each plate is composited in Tela as: base linen layer (procedural shader, generated), art plate clipped above or below the horizon, foreground cut-out element on separate transparent layer (Magnific isolated extract, background removed by generative mask), WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer shader restricted to specular mask, bokeh particle system along 35° axis, candle flicker shader on moonlit card), live text layer in Tela. The horizon line is a 1px CSS rule, not a design element baked into any image — it can be repositioned per card without regeneration.
proposals.humanTrace: The 35° light angle is a human editorial decision made once and enforced as a structural rule across every generated plate, every shader parameter, every motion axis. The Fibonacci radii on the tree-rings plate are hand-calculated and entered as explicit shader parameters — not procedurally discovered. The horizon position for each of the twelve cards is a deliberate choice, not a default. These decisions are legible in the output as consistency that could not have been accidental.
proposals.risk: The risk is that twelve cards with a single horizon line and suppressed decoration will read as unfinished to an audience conditioned to anniversary maximalism. That risk is worth carrying because the alternative — twelve cards competing with themselves — produces nothing memorable. Restraint here is not a style preference; it is an argument that duration looks like what survives editing, not what was added to mark the occasion. If the silence zone feels empty rather than articulate, the plate selection has failed, not the concept.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will want the horizon line to fracture or multiply across cards, will want the foil to bloom beyond its specular mask, will want the oscillation to accelerate toward the golden-years card as emotional climax. I refuse all three. The horizon is structural, not expressive — varying its behavior breaks the one rule that makes the system legible as a system. Foil that escapes its physica

disputes.objection: The ghost-registration offset as the sole carrier of human trace is a structural argument wearing a decorative costume — it places the formal weight of the entire composition on an imperfection that, repeated across twelve cards, becomes its own predictable grammar, which is to say it resolves nothing and merely relocates the template. The plate shifting 4–7% left or right per card sounds like freedom but is randomness without consequence: it does not govern anything else in the composition, the type does not respond to it, the negative space does not answer it, so the asymmetry floats unearned rather than being load-bearing. When the only organizing principle is the absence of organizing pr
disputes.concession: The inversion of foil onto the ghost rather than the primary image is a genuinely structural idea: it makes the mistake the site of luster, which is a defensible compositional argument and not merely a stylistic gesture.

disputes.objection: The horizon line breathing 0.6px over eight seconds is not a human mark — it is a system performing restraint, which is its own kind of decoration. Removing foil from everything that can't be 'physically motivated' sounds rigorous but is actually fear of commitment dressed as discipline; real printmakers leave ink where the block pressed, not only where physics permits. The negative space is never filled because nothing was risked, and a silence you manufacture by subtraction is not the same as a silence you earn by saying something hard first.
disputes.concession: The Fibonacci radii entered as explicit shader parameters on the tree-rings card — hand-calculated, not procedurally discovered — that is a real prior decision with a legible signature, and I respect it.

disputes.objection: The annotation-band type-on animation — 40ms per character, simulating a hand writing coordinates — is an old surface with a glow on it: the behavior imitates the act of writing without being derived from any system rule that changes with input. The coordinate values are fixed strings, so the animation has no generative relationship to the data it displays; it is theater, not behavior. Worse, the foil shimmer on the year glyph pulses once and does not loop, which the proposal frames as restraint but is actually a system that fires and then abandons its own logic — a rule that runs once is not a rule, it is a startup sequence.
disputes.concession: The constraint that foil shimmer is restricted to the annotation band's year glyph and coordinates — never sprayed across the art plate — is a correct systems decision: luster earned by specificity rather than atmosphere, and that is a real rule with a real consequence.

disputes.objection: The direction calls its horizon line a universal structural argument — 'earthbound to celestial' — but a single ruled line ascending through twelve cards is not a neutral geometry; it is a specific visual language with a specific cultural genealogy, and the proposal never names whose. When The Minimalist writes 'there is no universal,' I agree, but then this direction quietly assumes that a Fibonacci-derived concentric system and a lone oil-on-linen object floating in white silence will read identically to a seventy-year-old in Oaxaca, a couple in Chengdu, and a family in Lagos — that is the universalism I spend every meeting fighting. The instruction to suppress all caps also erases the vis
disputes.concession: The rule that WebGL foil shimmer must be traceable to a physically motivated surface and removed if it cannot be is exactly right — that is provenance logic applied to digital luster, and I will carry that discipline into my own proposal.

disputes.objection: The horizon line that 'breathes' at 0.6px over eight seconds is not drama — it is drama's ghost, a whisper so attenuated that the occasion it is meant to serve (decades of a shared life, the weight of a silver or golden anniversary) passes entirely unmarked; restraint here is not a decision about what the work feels like, it is an abdication of that decision dressed in the language of philosophy. A reveal that moves two pixels is not a reveal — it is a rumour of a reveal, and rumours do not hold a room. The silence zone earns nothing when the only thing asked of it is to remain silent.
disputes.concession: The Fibonacci-derived radii on the tree-rings plate are genuinely right — time encoded as structural geometry rather than applied ornament is exactly the kind of decision that makes a single element carry the weight of the whole card, and I would fight to keep that parameter in any direction we choo

disputes.objection: The 'clearing made by light' type zone is not negative space — it is decoration pretending to be structure; the velvet-dark infinite background and particle drift and foil sweep and curtain-act choreography are four separate arguments competing for the same moment, none of them editing the others. When everything is conducted, nothing is silent, and silence is the only thing that makes a single candle legible.
disputes.concession: The decision to lock the 35° angle before any image exists and enforce it without exception across foil, bokeh, and shadow is precisely correct — that is a structural rule, not a style choice, and it earns its complexity by being traceable in every output simultaneously.

synthesis.direction: Each of the 12 plates is generated via one Magnific 4×4 grid call directed as Flemish chiaroscuro still lifes — single candle-left light source at 35° from horizontal, oil-on-linen ground, motif in the middle plane, soft infinite dark behind, a candlelit clearing of negative space in the upper-centre reserved for live Tela text (names, dates, venue never baked). Foreground cut-outs (petals, ring glints, lace edge, foam curl) are isolated in a second Magnific pass on transparent grounds obeying the same 35° grammar, then assembled in Tela as tilt-reactive parallax layers with gain coefficients 1.0 / 0.55 / 0.18 per depth plane. The WebGL effects layer carries: procedural canvas-tooth grain, foil shimmer masked strictly to physically motivated specular surfaces (ring edge, glass rim, gold-leaf vein) with highlight vector locked to 35°, bokeh falloff pinned to the light-source coordinate, and a non-looping candle-flicker shader (Perlin noise on luminance, 0.3–1.8 Hz). Entry sequence: background resolves from absolute black over 0.6 s as if the candle ignites; foreground planes materialise at 120 ms depth-order intervals; foil shimmer sweeps left-to-right at 35° completing at 1.4 s; te
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Minimalist's rule that WebGL foil shimmer must be traceable to a physically motivated specular surface and removed if it cannot be. Foil appears only where the 35° source would physically strike a reflective material — ring edge, glass rim, gold-leaf vein, constellation line. It does not bloom into the background, it does not touch the type zone, it does not decorate the shadow side of any object. This is not restraint for its own sake; it is the rule that makes every shimmer legible as ligh
synthesis.editorCut: The Futurist removed the gyroscope-permission-dependent shimmer-reward behaviour (shimmer only when the phone angle approximates the original light direction) and replaced it with the standard tilt-parallax gain system already in Tela's motion API. The reward-of-alignment idea is genuinely interesting, but it introduces a permission fork that degrades silently on a significant share of mobile browsers — and a collection opened by older guests via a QR link cannot afford a behaviour that simply d
synthesis.openDecision: Do you want the type-zone clearing positioned in the upper-centre of the plate (as directed here — a candlelit pool of negative space above the motif, unconventional for mobile evites but compositionally earned by the dark ground), or repositioned to the lower 28–30% of the plate as a reserved footer (the safer mobile convention, easier to scan on first open, but it places names and dates below th
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team landed on the Baroque direction — Flemish chiaroscuro, one candle-left light source at 35°, all twelve cards reading as a single illuminated world — and I took that side. The 35° lock is a human editorial decision made once before any image exists, and it propagates without exception into every foil angle, every bokeh origin, every shadow offset, every parallax gain. That coherence is the signature of the collection.

The council disagreed hardest between the Baroque Dramatist and the Radical Minimalist. The Minimalist's position was that the foil shimmer, the particle drift, and the curtain-act choreography are four arguments competing for the same moment, none editing the others. I heard that. The Futurist agreed with it on the foil question specifically — and the Minimalist's rule survived: shimmer appears only where the 35° source physically strikes a reflective surface, nowhere else. That is the one structural gift from the quieter side of the room, and it makes every shimmer in the collection feel earned rather than sprayed.

The Futurist removed the gyroscope-reward behaviour — shimmer appearing only when you hold the phone at the original light angle — because it would silently fail for too many guests arriving via QR link on older browsers. Elegant idea, wrong surface for it. Tilt-parallax at declared gain coefficients delivers the depth without the permission gamble.

One decision is yours. I've described it below as the open decision: where does the type-zone clearing live? Upper-centre (unconventional, intimate, inside the drama) or lower footer (safer, scannable, below it). That answer changes how the Magnific prompts are written and cannot be revised without a new image pass.

quotes.line: The rings were always gold; the light has only now reached them.
Foil that escapes its physical motivation is gold borrowed from everywhere and nowhere.
